title: Exhaustive Decider for Bounded Runs
statement: For every finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ over the binary alphabet, there are a finite deterministic Turing machine $E$ over that alphabet and a natural number $C$ such that the following holds for every binary input $z$ and $T\in\mathbb{N}$. If every branch of $N$ on $z$ has halted within $T$ steps, then $E$ computes the output $[1]$ within exactly $C2^{C(T+1)}$ steps when $N$ accepts $z$ within $T$ steps, and computes $[0]$ within exactly that many steps when $N$ does not accept $z$ within $T$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: N is a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over Bool
Every choice word of length T leads N on z to a halted configuration
